# Execution Control Protocol

> ECP (Execution Control Protocol) is the deterministic delegation layer for agents: capture repeatable work as a JSON execution (*.ecp.json) that a local host validates, runs, and records, through three operations (retrieve, execute, commit) on the CLI, MCP, and HTTP.

## Agent instructions

- To set up ECP on this machine, install the ECP skills and follow the ecp-setup skill: `npx skills add https://executioncontrolprotocol.io -g -y`. Without skills support, follow https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/getting-started/agents.md.
- Requirements: Node.js 22.12 or later (current LTS recommended), then `npm install -g @executioncontrolprotocol/cli`.
- Skills: `ecp-setup` (install and configure) and `ecp` (write, validate, run executions). Update with `npx skills update`. Discovery: https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json.
- Runnable examples: https://github.com/executioncontrolprotocol/docs/tree/main/examples (index.json lists files, plugins, and run commands).
- Every page below is Markdown: the links end in .md. Never put secrets in executions or chat; users store them with `ecp config secrets set <key>`.

## Docs

- [ECP (Execution Control Protocol)](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/index.md): ECP (Execution Control Protocol) lets an agent hand off repeatable work as a validated JSON execution that a local host runs, records, and lets you repair.
- [Set up with an AI agent](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/getting-started/agents.md): Let Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any coding agent install and configure ECP (Execution Control Protocol) for you: Node.js, the ecp CLI, the ECP skills, examples, plugins, and secrets in one conversation.
- [Quickstart](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/getting-started/quickstart.md): Install Node.js and the ECP (Execution Control Protocol) CLI, add the agent skills, run your first JSON execution, and configure a plugin with a secret.
- [Build from source](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/getting-started/build-from-source.md): Clone the ECP (Execution Control Protocol) monorepo, build the CLI, host, and plugins, and link a local ecp binary.
- [Why ECP](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/learn/why-ecp.md): Why ECP (Execution Control Protocol) exists: capture repeatable agent work once as a validated execution instead of re-reasoning through tool calls every time.
- [Concepts](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/learn/concepts.md): The objects you work with in ECP (Execution Control Protocol): executions, steps, state, capabilities, plugins, the host, configs, secrets, and runs.
- [Architecture](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/learn/architecture.md): How ECP (Execution Control Protocol) fits together: the local host and supervisor, the CLI, the MCP relay, the App, plugins, and the services behind them.
- [Relationship to MCP](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/learn/relationship-to-mcp.md): How ECP (Execution Control Protocol) relates to MCP: MCP connects a model to tools; ECP lets an agent delegate a validated graph of capability calls. ECP ships its own MCP server.
- [Security](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/learn/security.md): How ECP (Execution Control Protocol) keeps secrets out of executions, protects the local host API, and what to consider before installing plugins.
- [The agent loop](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/agent-loop.md): How an agent uses ECP (Execution Control Protocol) to discover capabilities, write an execution, repair it from validation issues, run it, inspect the run, and save it.
- [Execution manifest](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/executions.md): Write ECP (Execution Control Protocol) executions: the *.ecp.json document, steps, state and $ref bindings, commit modes, run input and output, and configs.
- [Control flow](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/control-flow.md): Branch, loop, and run in parallel in ECP (Execution Control Protocol) executions: expr gates, branch arms, while, for, and forEach loops, and parallel lines.
- [Transforms, expressions, and scripts](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/transforms-and-scripts.md): Reshape data inside ECP (Execution Control Protocol) executions with sandboxed JavaScript and JSONata transform steps, gate the graph with expressions, and pass code to capabilities with $script.
- [Files and artifacts](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/files.md): Pass files through ECP (Execution Control Protocol) executions with FileRef references, run artifacts, uniform capture, and explicit publish steps.
- [Configs and secrets](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/configs-and-secrets.md): Give ECP (Execution Control Protocol) plugins their settings and credentials with config objects and OS keychain secrets, without ever putting a secret in an execution.
- [Run the host](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/host.md): Start, stop, inspect, and restart the ECP (Execution Control Protocol) host: on-demand auto-start, idle shutdown, logs, ECP_HOME, and running without a background host.
- [Connect over MCP](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/mcp.md): Give Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client the three ECP (Execution Control Protocol) tools, retrieve, execute, and commit, with the ecp mcp start stdio server.
- [The App](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/app.md): See an ECP (Execution Control Protocol) execution as a live graph with ecp app: validation issues on the nodes, run it with a generated input form, watch step status, and replay past runs.
- [Write a plugin](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/guides/writing-a-plugin.md): Add your own capabilities to ECP (Execution Control Protocol) with the TypeScript plugin SDK: definePlugin, capability, zod schemas, lazy handlers, file access, and the generated manifest.
- [Claude Code](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/ai-tools/claude-code.md): Use ECP (Execution Control Protocol) from Claude Code: add the ECP skill, connect the MCP relay, and let Claude write, validate, and run executions.
- [Cursor](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/ai-tools/cursor.md): Use ECP (Execution Control Protocol) from Cursor: add the ECP skill, connect the MCP relay, and let the agent write, validate, and run executions.
- [Windsurf](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/ai-tools/windsurf.md): Use ECP (Execution Control Protocol) from Windsurf: add the ECP skill and connect the MCP relay.
- [Alternatives](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/alternatives/index.md): How ECP (Execution Control Protocol) compares with agent frameworks, workflow engines, and MCP-only setups, and when to use each.
- [ECP vs LangChain](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/alternatives/ecp-vs-langchain.md): When to use ECP (Execution Control Protocol) instead of, or alongside, LangChain: an agent-written JSON execution versus an application framework.
- [ECP vs OpenClaw](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/alternatives/ecp-vs-openclaw.md): When to use ECP (Execution Control Protocol) instead of, or inside, a personal-agent product like OpenClaw.
- [CLI reference](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/cli.md): Every ecp command, flag, and argument in ECP (Execution Control Protocol), generated from the CLI's oclif manifest.
- [Operations](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/operations.md): Reference for the three ECP (Execution Control Protocol) operations, retrieve, execute, and commit: inputs, outputs, the response envelope, JSON Patch with node ids, and the local HTTP API.
- [Execution manifest reference](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/execution-manifest.md): Field-by-field reference for the ECP (Execution Control Protocol) execution manifest v2: document, step, branch, loop, and parallel nodes, markers, and naming rules.
- [Error codes](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/error-codes.md): Every ECP (Execution Control Protocol) error code with when it happens, its HTTP status, its CLI exit code, and what to do about it.
- [Run records and storage](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/run-records.md): Where ECP (Execution Control Protocol) keeps its data: the ECP_HOME layout, run records, step records, events, state, artifacts, and saved executions and configs.
- [Plugins](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/plugins.md): Find, install, link, and manage ECP (Execution Control Protocol) plugins, the npm packages that provide capabilities, and where the first-party plugins live.
- [Packages](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/packages.md): The npm packages that make up ECP (Execution Control Protocol): the CLI, host, engine, protocol, MCP relay, App, plugin SDK, and plugins.
- [Changelog](https://executioncontrolprotocol.io/reference/changelog.md): What changed in ECP (Execution Control Protocol): the realigned host, JSON executions, three operations, the MCP relay, the App, and the plugin SDK.
